action.objective: Convert the winning endgame by centralizing the bishop on e5, keeping the rook active, and advancing the passed a-pawn.
action.rationale: d4e5 is the only commit-ready move: depth-4 exact score 932, complete safety check with no mating reply, tactical_refutation not_found. It attacks e7 and c7 while the rook on e4 supports the bishop (geometric defender), so a simple Rxe5 trade would leave White with a favorable rook endgame. Alternative e4f4 scored 926 at depth 4 but its safety was not independently verified; the 6-point gap is within noise, so I keep the verified move with concrete evidence. Black's likely f7g6 keeps the king passive while White plays a5a6 and pushes the passed pawn.
